rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination - Source of Income Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords in New Jersey cannot refuse to rent to a tenant solely because they use a lawful source of income, such as a Section 8 housing voucher, to pay rent.
rules.key_value: Prohibits denial of housing based on lawful source of income
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to sale or rental of all property, including open land, for business or residential purposes, with limited exceptions for small owner-occupied dwellings and religious organization preferences.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious organization preference for same-religion tenants/buyers; housing for older persons exempt from familial status provisions.
rules.citation: N.J. Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the owner occupies a unit in a two-family dwelling or a one-family dwelling being rented out in part

rules.conflict_note: Specific statutory section number for the source-of-income provision is not stated in this chunk; the general LAD citation is used based on the text's reference to the law and to N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm for a related definition.
